clue.text: One who sits on heavy horse

parts.note: a percher is one who sits, as a bird sits on a branch

explanation.surface: A rider settles onto the back of a big draught horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the last two words; 'on' is taken as written, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Percheron is a breed of large French draught horse, an example of a heavy horse.

clue.text: Academic keeps old evidence

indicators.note: the academic keeps, so holds within himself, the letter for old

parts.note: a prof, short for professor, is an academic

explanation.surface: A lecturer hangs on to ancient documents that prove a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof is a synonym for evidence that establishes a fact.

clue.text: Foreign national encounters obstacle en route to suicidal undertaking

parts.note: a Russian is a national of a foreign country

indicators.note: en is French for in, so the obstacle goes in the word route

parts.note: a let is an obstacle, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A traveller from abroad hits a snag on the road to a reckless venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'en route' looks like one phrase, but 'en' is French for in and works as the container signal. 'encounters' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Russian roulette, spinning a revolver with one bullet and firing at oneself, is a byword for a suicidal undertaking.

clue.text: Not paying attention — it's unnecessary to replace nitrogen by hydrogen

indicators.note: the hydrogen is brought in to replace, or take the place of, the nitrogen

parts.note: needless means unnecessary
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A careless chemist says swapping one gas for another serves no purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedless means careless, failing to take heed or notice, so not paying attention.

clue.text: Implement set at a sloping angle

definitions.meaning: to ... a stage or seat is to set it on a slope

explanation.surface: A tool is fixed on a tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Rake is both a garden tool and, as a verb, to incline something from the vertical or horizontal.

clue.text: Northern Ireland soldier, a redcap, adding nothing to operation he's a fool

parts.note: an NCO is a non-commissioned officer, a soldier
redcap is slang for a military policeman, an MP
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: An Ulster squaddie and a military policeman bungle a mission and are branded idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: A redcap is British slang for a military policeman, from their red-topped caps. 'adding ... to' just strings the pieces on; 'he's a' leads to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nincompoop is a silly, foolish person, a synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Intensity apparent in small subdivision connected with hospital

parts.note: dept, short for department, is a small form of the word for a subdivision
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A section of a hospital shows a certain fervour.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth can mean intensity, as in depth of feeling or of colour.

clue.text: Stew — cooked it herself — you can see it there

indicators.note: the answer can be seen there, spelt out across the words cooked it herself

explanation.surface: Someone serves a casserole they made themselves, inviting you to look.
explanation.definitionFit: To stew is to fret or be agitated, as is to dither in an indecisive flap.

clue.text: Unusually cracking sports downing hot snacks

indicators.note: the jumbled letters down, or swallow, the letter for hot
the letters are arranged in an unusual order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Excited sportsmen gulp hot nibbles after a remarkable game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' gives the anagram (PORKSCRATCINGS) and 'downing' takes in the H. Pork scratchings are a British pub snack of crisp fried pork rind.
explanation.definitionFit: Pork scratchings, fried crunchy pieces of pork skin, are snacks sold in British pubs.

clue.text: Was reluctant, he said, to swallow iodine

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for said is to swallow, or take in, the letter for iodine

parts.note: stated means said
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A man claims he didn't want to take his iodine medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitated means paused through doubt, so held back or was reluctant.

clue.text: Coming to a head surrounded by monsters, grotesque, but friendly enough

indicators.note: the climax word is surrounded by the jumbled monster letters
grotesque suggests a misshapen, distorted form of the word monsters

parts.note: peaking means reaching a climax, coming to a head

explanation.surface: Ugly beasts gather round a crisis yet remain on decent terms with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grotesque' gives ONSTERMS, the anagram, which 'surrounded by' wraps round the other piece. 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on speaking terms means being friendly enough to talk, though perhaps not close.

clue.text: Quite without bias

definitions.meaning: ... means quite or moderately, as in ... good

explanation.surface: Moderately free from prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairly means both moderately and justly, without prejudice.

clue.text: County needing a few runs prepared for action

parts.note: some means a few
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
set means ready, prepared for action

explanation.surface: A county cricket side needs only a handful of runs and is ready to go.
explanation.walkthrough: SOMERSET is a county in south-west England. 'needing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is an English county, so an example of a county.

clue.text: With no energy dancing hornpipes is unlikely in this hulk

indicators.note: the letters dance about into a new order
with no energy means the letter for energy is taken away

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lethargic sailors are unlikely to dance a jig aboard this old vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no' removes E from HORNPIPES; 'dancing' shuffles HORNPIPS plus IS. A hulk is an old ship used as a prison; 'unlikely in this' only links the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Hulks were old dismasted ships moored and used as floating gaols, so a hulk is this kind of vessel.

clue.text: What's written when football club shares start to tumble

parts.note: Man U is short for Manchester United football club
scrip is a certificate for shares, or shares themselves

indicators.note: the start of tumble is its first letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports that a football club's stock is beginning to fall.
explanation.walkthrough: Man U is Manchester United, the English football club. 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A manuscript is a document written by hand or before printing, so what's written.

clue.text: Tiny proportion of potato produced in Silicon Valley?

parts.note: micro means tiny
a chip is a portion cut from a potato

explanation.surface: A small bit of fried potato is said to come from California's tech hub.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the definition by example: Silicon Valley is famous for making silicon chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Microchips are the semiconductor circuits made by the firms of Silicon Valley in California.

clue.text: Document starts off with really intriguing theory

indicators.note: the starts of each following word are taken off and joined

explanation.surface: A paper begins with a truly fascinating hypothesis.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal written legal document, an order from a court.

clue.text: Move quickly to cover deficit up, but go into liquidation

indicators.note: the word for move quickly is to cover, or go round, the other piece

parts.note: to dive is to move quickly, plunge

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a loss is a deficit

explanation.surface: A firm rushes to cover its debts but ends up bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LOSS into SSOL, which DIVE covers. The surface points to business failure; the definition means melt into liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissolve is literally to pass into solution, so to go into liquid form.

clue.text: Produce a whip

definitions.meaning: a riding ... is a short whip

explanation.surface: Farm output and a riding whip.
explanation.definitionFit: Crop means both a harvest of produce and a short riding whip.

clue.text: Went about with depleted task force beginning to climb Greek mountain after setback

indicators.note: after a setback everything assembled is turned back, read in reverse
depleted means reduced, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a detail is a small detachment of troops given a particular task

indicators.note: the beginning of climb is its first letter

parts.note: Ossa is a mountain in Thessaly, Greece

explanation.surface: A weakened expedition team starts to ascend a Greek peak after a reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depleted' drops the final L, leaving DETAI; 'after setback' then turns the whole string DETAICOSSA back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To associate with someone is to keep company or go about with them.

clue.text: Band always walk ostentatiously …

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn round the waist or over the shoulder
ay, or aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A ribbon-wearing beauty queen always struts about.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 21 down only for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To sashay is to walk in a showy, swaggering or flouncing way.

clue.text: Medium pilot in a spin

indicators.note: a spin throws the letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aviator is sent into a tailspin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' looks like part of the indicator but is fodder; 'spin' alone rearranges PILOTINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil paint is a medium in the artistic sense, the material an artist works in.

clue.text: Ask the man regularly in complaint

indicators.note: regularly means every third letter is dropped at a steady interval

explanation.surface: Question the fellow routinely about his illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Write out ASKTHEMAN and drop every third letter, K, E and N, to keep the rest. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a respiratory illness, and complaint is a common word for an ailment.

clue.text: … when, for instance, there's a test

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
say means for instance, for example

explanation.surface: Continuing 18, someone strutting is put to the test.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening ellipsis links back to 18 down for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: An assay is a test, especially of a metal's purity.

clue.text: Deep sea fish

definitions.meaning: low in pitch, deep in sound
a perch-like fish of the sea

explanation.surface: A fish from the depths of the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Bass means a deep voice or note and also names a type of sea fish.

clue.text: Do something newsworthy — use anti-wrinkle treatment?

definitions.meaning: whimsically, to attack the lines on one's head, such as forehead wrinkles

explanation.surface: Grab the headlines by using a beauty cream.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to become front-page news, and read literally it means to strike at the lines on your head.

clue.text: Verse writer's unknown

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer, so writer's gives Poe's
Y is a mathematical unknown, like X

explanation.surface: Poetry by an anonymous author.
explanation.definitionFit: Poesy is an old word for poetry, which is verse.

clue.text: Press bays for punishment for people unlike the good Samaritan

indicators.note: punishment suggests the letters are knocked about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Journalists' howls of protest demand retribution against callous bystanders.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible parable, priests and Levites passed by the injured man while the good Samaritan stopped to help.
explanation.definitionFit: Passers-by in the parable walked past the wounded traveller, unlike the good Samaritan who helped him.
